Bug_Title: NP: Null value is guaranteed to be dereferenced (NP_GUARANTEED_DEREF)
Bug_Details:
There is a statement or branch that if executed guarantees that
      a value is null at this point, and that
      value that is guaranteed to be dereferenced
      (except on forward paths involving runtime exceptions).
       Note that a check such as
    if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException();
    is treated as a dereference of x. if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException(); x
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method. We're trying to dereference the buggyString variable without checking if it's null. This can lead to a NullPointerException if buggyString is null.
Trigger_Explanation: The test method testShowBug_nullString does not set the buggyString field of the NullDereferenceBug object before calling the showBug method. This leads to a NullPointerException when showBug tries to dereference buggyString.
